messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into German, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE German line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑conditions) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|------------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------|--------| | ove | locative adverb introducing a place‑clause (“where”) | wo | where | OK | | udirai | future 2nd sg of *udire* – “you will hear” | hören wirst | will hear | OK | | le | definite article, fem. pl – marks *strida* as specific | die | the (pl.) | OK | | disperate | adjective, fem. pl – “desperate, despairing” | verzweifelten | desperate | OK | | strida | noun, fem. pl – “shrieks” | Schreie | shrieks | OK | | vedrai | future 2nd sg of *vedere* – “you will see” | wirst sehen | will see | OK | | li | definite article, masc. pl – marks *spiriti* as specific | die | the (pl.) | OK | | antichi | adjective, masc. pl – “ancient, old” | alten | ancient | OK | | spiriti | noun, masc. pl – “spirits” | Geister | spirits | OK | | dolenti | adjective, masc. pl – “woeful, lamenting” | klagenden | woeful | OK | | ch’ (che) | relative pronoun introducing a clause – “who/that” | die | who | OK | | a | preposition “to, toward” | zum | to the (dative) | OK | | la | definite article, fem. sg – marks *morte* as specific | — (absorbed in *zum*) | the | UNNECESSARY | | seconda | ordinal adjective, fem. sg – “second” | zweiten | second | OK | | morte | noun, fem. sg – “death” | Tod | death | OK | | ciascun | distributive pronoun – “each” | jeder | each | OK | | grida | verb, 3rd sg present – “shouts, cries out” | schreien wird | will shout | OK |
---
### Items to Review - **UNNECESSARY:** *la* – the Italian feminine singular article has no separate counterpart in German; its function is subsumed in the prepositional phrase *zum* (“to the”). - **MISSING / WRONG / GRAMMAR:** none detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only German script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final German text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 115: - Original: wo du die verzweifelten Schreie hören wirst, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change - Line 116: - Original: du wirst die alten klagenden Geister sehen, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change - Line 117: - Original: die jeder zum zweiten Tod schreien wird; - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
